findings.title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The dataclass field is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`, so Python calls timezone.now() once when the class is defined/imported and reuses that same value as the default for every AssignmentSource created during the process lifetime. All instances will therefore report the (stale) process-start time instead of their creation time. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets a fresh timestamp.

findings.title: Datetime in AssignmentSource.to_dict() is not JSON-serializable for the Celery task
findings.body: assignment_source.to_dict() uses dataclasses.asdict(), which leaves `queued` as a datetime object. sync_group_assignee_outbound then passes that dict as `assignment_source_dict` in sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...). Celery/Kombu serializes task kwargs as JSON, and a datetime is not JSON serializable, so enqueueing the outbound task will raise a serialization/EncodeError whenever an inbound webhook supplied an assignment_source (exactly the new code path). This propagates out of GroupAssignee.assign/deassign called from sync_group_assignee_inbound, breaking inbound assignment; the eager `self.tasks()` tests do not serialize kwargs, so they do not catch it. Serialize `queued` to an ISO string in to_dict() (and parse it back in from_dict()) or drop it from the wire format.

findings.title: from_dict does not validate/coerce field types, so malformed payloads can silently disable cycle prevention
findings.body: from_dict only catches ValueError/TypeError from the constructor call. A payload such as {"source_name": 123, "integration_id": "456", "queued": "not-a-date"} constructs successfully with wrongly-typed fields; integration_id as a string will never equal the integer org_integration.integration_id in IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync, so the sync-cycle guard is silently bypassed and the loop the PR aims to prevent can recur. Coerce/validate integration_id (and queued) explicitly and return None (or raise) on type mismatches.
